pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Adds support for Object/Label detection and Face detection/identification via AWS Rekognition. Also adds service to index (train) faces.
As I saw mentioned in the previous PR #22803, this PR aligns with the existing AWS component and utilises the included boto async libraries.


## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box! 
  If your PR requires multiple boxes to be checked, you'll most likely need to
  split it into multiple PRs. This makes things easier and faster to code review.
-->

- Dependency upgrade
- Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- New integration (thank you!)
- [X] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)
- Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml`:
<!--
  Supplying a configuration snippet, makes it easier for a maintainer to test
  your PR. Furthermore, for new integrations, it gives an impression of how
  the configuration would look like.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR does not have an example entry.
-->

Below contains a full-form configuration for face identification and a short-form configuration for object detection.

Note that face detection requires a Rekognition face 'collection' to be created to reference below, it will be created if it doesn't already exist.

```yaml
# Example configuration.yaml
aws:
  image_processing:
    - platform: face
      service: rekognition
      region_name: ap-southeast-2
      collection_id: family
      identify_faces: true
      save_file_folder: /path/to/detection_images
      save_file_timestamp: true
      confidence: 90
      source:
        - entity_id: camera.local_file
        - entity_id: camera.entrance_doorway
      detection_attributes: ALL
    - platform: object
      service: rekognition
      region_name: ap-southeast-2
      source:
        - entity_id: camera.local_file
```

## Additional information
<!--
  Details are important, and help maintainers processing your PR.
  Please be sure to fill out additional details, if applicable.
-->

pr_comments: @robmarkcole - I would really appreciate your feedback on this as well, if possible. Your component and PR was a massive help for parsing and and saving the object data and I borrowed from it heavily, would be great to include your ROI and label whitelisting one day too 👍

I have added a check that `collection_id` exists and create if not. I will detail IAM permissions required in the docs.
I think it would also be useful to add a `train_face` service similar to other components (apologies to drag this PR out).

Would look similar to this (process all images in folder as `person1`):

```yaml
Service: aws.rekognition_train_face
Data:
  entity_id: image_processing.rekognition_face_entity
  folder: face_images/person1
  image_id: person1
```

Optional to include image_path instead (single image as `person1`):

```yaml
Service: aws.rekognition_train_face
Data:
  entity_id: image_processing.rekognition_face_entity
  image_path: face_images/person1.jpg
  image_id: person1
```

I made a couple of suggestions for refactoring const out to pil helpers etc but this is just a suggestion and can wait. Is test coverage causing the codecov/patch error? In my experience the senior reviewers only jump in once this test coverage is met. Some aspects are hard to test, like the annotating of images so perhaps this is a special case.

Truly appreciate the assistance @robmarkcole it's been a massive help! It's mostly just code coverage that is causing the failed tests but I think it's possible to meet the coverage requirement and is a good goal to make regardless so will continue trying to bump that up, not far off.

Apologies @pvizeli, that was my reading comprehension failing me. I thought it was a little strange to require all functions in a component to be async but that is what I thought reading the following line in the docs. Reading it again I can obviously see that's not the case. My bad 😅 

`Home Assistant uses the convention that all functions that must be run from within the event loop are prefixed with async_.`

Regardless I've fixed that up, made changes to the docs and looking at the codecov report I'm pretty happy that I've covered everything relevant for the integration. Feel free to review when possible 👍
@robmarkcole - apologies for the late response, I missed your message. I've updated the tests for increased coverage 👍

which leads me to believe somehow, the aws_secret_access_key and aws_access_key_id are not getting passed.
I'm running this in python3 of same HA container, so it seems like the same versions of botocore/aiobotocore stuff is working fine otherwise.

I think i see the issue, but just started messing with home-assistant and am not sure i'd be a great person to put up a PR with the fix. I think the main problem is around here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/master/homeassistant/components/aws/__init__.py#L162-L170

If a profile is used then the boto session has it associated with it and future sdk calls will use it. If a profile isn't used then the parameter-less constructor is hit and i imagine that would only have any auth associated with it if creds existed in `AWS_` env vars or if the default profile existed. This doesn't fail the cred validation though because `**aws_config` is passed in and the `client` constructor also accepts those aws cred params. 

In the `async_get_services` def `**aws_config` is passed to the client constructor, but is created from `discovery_info` ( https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/master/homeassistant/components/aws/notify.py#L48 ) and that seems to be equal to the `notify` section of the configuration and not the `credentials` bit. I tested by setting my configuration.yml to this and things seem to work:
```
aws:
  credentials:
    - name: default
      aws_access_key_id: !secret aws_access_key
      aws_secret_access_key: !secret aws_secret_key
      validate: true
  notify:
    - service: sns
      region_name: us-west-2
      credential_name: default
      aws_access_key_id: !secret aws_access_key
      aws_secret_access_key: !secret aws_secret_key
```

Potentially the creds exist in `async_get_service` in the `config` arg and could be passed along from there, but i think that it makes more sense to associate them with the session created in `_validate_aws_credentials`

Fix might just be:
```
    if profile is not None:
        session = aiobotocore.AioSession(profile=profile)
        del aws_config[CONF_PROFILE_NAME]
        if CONF_ACCESS_KEY_ID in aws_config:
            del aws_config[CONF_ACCESS_KEY_ID]
        if CONF_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in aws_config:
            del aws_config[CONF_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY]
    else:
        session = aiobotocore.AioSession(**aws_config)
```

but I'm not sure if the `CONF_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`CONF_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` keys should be removed from the dict or what the down stream effects of that might be. I'm guessing that is done in the session+profile logic so that a specified profile isn't overriden by creds on accident

in my variant I am using object_detected which I feel is a more natural description. However I realise you are being consistent with detect_face
Completely agree `object_detected` and `face_detected` is much more natural, but with `detect_face` coming from the base component I think consistency wins in this scenario

The expression 'two wrongs do not make a right' comes to mind :)
In this case a breaking change is inevitable for some users:

1) Use of `detect_object` is a breaking change for the users of [my custom integration](https://github.com/robmarkcole/HASS-amazon-rekognition),. Also its then incompatible with my [deepstack integration](https://github.com/robmarkcole/HASS-Deepstack-object) which I plan on making official soon. Combining stars on those two projects estimate 200 users affected.
2) Use `object_detected` and update the face integration to use `face_detected`.
